title: Why Harder? Moment of Inertia Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A heavy door is slow to start swinging. A merry-go-round full of children is hard to get turning. And Diya finds a metre ruler spins easily about its middle but is hard to swing about its end. Same ruler, same mass. So what changed? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we meet moment of inertia, the turning version of mass.

On a live motion notebook a light rod with two 1 kg balls spins with 1 joule of energy, while the readout tracks r, I, omega and the speed of the far ball, and a graph shows I climbing as the axis slides from the middle to the end. A slow-mo replay shows v = r omega. We derive K = half I omega squared step by step from kinetic energy, see link by link why the end is harder, compare balls close in and pushed out side by side, and work out I and the kinetic energy of a spinning rod. Then the exam trap (r is measured from the axis), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.

In this video:
0:00 Why is a ruler harder to spin by its end?
0:28 Inertia for turning: I = sum of m r squared
0:57 Motion notebook: a spinning rod
1:17 Slow-mo replay: v = r omega
1:28 Slide the axis: I doubles
1:48 Pause and think: is I fixed?
2:03 K = half I omega squared, in 4 steps
2:54 Why the end is harder, link by link
3:16 Close in vs pushed out + pause and think
3:50 Worked example: I and kinetic energy
4:23 Exam trap: measure r from the axis
4:44 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:21 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Radius of Gyration and Moments of Inertia of Common Bodies. A ring and a disc, same mass, same push. Which one spins up faster?
